entities.name: Imperial War Museum London
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Imperial War Museum (IWM) in London, founded 1917 during World War I by Sir Alfred Mond to record and exhibit material related to British and Imperial military operations — initially conceived as a record of WWI but expanded to cover all conflicts involving Britain from 1914 to the present — is now a network of five museums and the UK's primary institution for documenting the human experience of war. The London branch occupies the former Bethlem Royal Hospital (Bedlam) — the world's most famous psychiatric institution — giving the museum a building with its own harrowing history.

The IWM was founded in 1917, unprecedented — a museum established during an ongoing conflict to document it in real time, including from all perspectives (military, civilian, enemy). The collection now exceeds 23 million items: 20 million documents and photographs, 33,000 art works (including the largest collection of WWI art anywhere), and major holdings of film and sound archives. Paul Nash's 'We Are Making a New World' and Christopher Nevinson's 'Paths of Glory' — key images of WWI's industrial horror — are at IWM.

The IWM's Holocaust Exhibition (2000) is considered the best Holocaust exhibition outside of Israel, using personal testimony to document the progression from discrimination through deportation to extermination. The Visitors' atrium now displays a V-2 rocket, a Spitfire, and the Enigma machine. IWM Duxford (Cambridgeshire) is Europe's premier aviation museum; HMS Belfast (moored on the Thames) documents WWII naval warfare. The IWM's 'Lives of the First World War' digital memorial catalogued 8 million WWI service records.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Imperial War Museum — founded during WWI itself, housing 23 million items including the largest WWI art collection, and containing the best Holocaust exhibition outside Israel — is the world's most comprehensive institution for documenting the human experience of modern war.
